Alex Carter: Quick sync — proposal to use per-token SNR sampling to prioritize calibration data for FP8/INT8/4-bit profiles. sketch: sample tokens with low SNR under target quant and run selective re-calibration. thoughts?
Priya Sharma: love the idea. curious about the sampling budget and how we avoid dataset leakage for private customers.
Mateo Ruiz: agree with budget concern. also need a clear metric: is SNR the only signal or do we add logit sensitivity / perplexity jump?
Casey Li: strong +1 on combining signals. my metric suggestion: SNR + delta-LL normalized by token freq. low freq but high delta should get priority.
Lana Gomez: operational question — where does this live? model-side telemetry or offline cal job? we need to avoid adding p50 latency overhead.
Alex Carter: runtime collects lightweight per-token counters (counts, sumsq logits) in an anonymized rolling buffer, then offline job pulls aggregated bins. no raw text leaves hosts.
Jing Wu: that helps for privacy. how big is the buffer? and how do we pick threshold? can we make it adaptive per-model & ctx-length?
Priya Sharma: propose sampling budget config: {"budget_tokens_per_minute": "int"} per deployment tier. thresholds adjusted by historical variance; run an LR to map variance->threshold.
Mateo Ruiz: experiment plan: A/B on canary traffic with `calib-on` vs `calib-off` using holdout prompts. Track delta accuracy on eval set + unit-cost change. small-scale first.
Casey Li: pseudo command for local testing:
```bash
# sample low-SNR tokens from logs
python tools/sample_snr.py --model rdx-13b --window 1024 --budget 50000 --out low_snr.json
# run selective calibration job
python tools/selective_calib.py --input low_snr.json --quant int8 --out profile_v2.json
```
Lana Gomez: ops-bot can we add a quota guard so sampling doesn't spike IO? ops-bot: quota guard implemented as token-leaky-bucket per-host, configured at 1e5 tokens/min by default.
ops-bot: Note: sampling jobs will be throttled if host CPU > 70% or disk IO > 60%. See /infra/ops/sampling-guards.
Jing Wu: how do we validate quality regression risk? I want a regression matrix: per-endpoint delta by prompt-type (few-shot, longctx, code).
Alex Carter: agreed. we'll generate a small eval harness that splits by use-case buckets and computes: delta-BLEU (for code), delta-ROUGE, delta-perplexity, and a simple human-ish acceptability score from existing evals.
Priya Sharma: timeline suggestion: week1 prototype (sampling + offline calib), week2 run canary on internal traffic, week3 expand to beta customers with opt-in, week4 rollback/patch based on results.
Mateo Ruiz: one more tradeoff: calibrating from low-SNR tokens might overfit rare artifacts. need holdout and regularization (mix with uniform samples).
Casey Li: +1 mix-in strategy. also cap max-profile-change-per-deploy to avoid big swings.
Lana Gomez: will coordinate with infra to add guard rails and telemetry dashboards. I'll add a chart for tokens-sampled/min and calibration delta per-rollout.
Alex Carter: sweet. next action items: Priya to write config schema; Mateo & Casey to mock eval harness; Jing & Lana to draft ops guard doc. I'll open the RFC followup with links.
Priya Sharma: I'll put the config schema in the PR: https://redwood.internal/r/quant-snr-proto (WIP) :memo:
Mateo Ruiz: I'll draft the eval notebooks, pinging team when ready.
Casey Li: I'll wire the cap on profile changes into the rollout controller.
Jing Wu: will add regression matrix template.
Lana Gomez: adding dashboards and sampling guard playbook.
Alex Carter: thanks all :thumbsup:
